intro.title: JWT Storage & Decode in React
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application that securely stores a JSON Web Token (JWT) in the browser's localStorage and decodes it to display user information. You will learn the core concept of handling authentication tokens in a client-side application, including storage and data extraction. The main technologies involved are React hooks like useState and useEffect, the localStorage API, and the jwt-decode library. By the end, you'll understand how to manage user sessions by safely storing tokens and accessing their payload data without sending them to a server.
intro.usecase: In real-world React applications, JWT storage and decoding is essential for user authentication and authorization. When users log into platforms like e-commerce sites, banking dashboards, or project management tools, their JWT tokens are stored locally to maintain sessions. Developers decode these tokens to display user-specific content, such as personalized dashboards, role-based navigation menus, or secure payment forms. This pattern ensures secure, persistent user experiences without requiring constant re-authentication.
